DREAM↔n_TOF matching: an outside audit

2026-08-13 · covers pulse_match.py, bunch_join.py, coincidence_arbiter.py, arbiter_measure.py, clock_qa.py, the dashboard, and the 08-13 recovery campaign state

Verdict: the physics is solved; the process is over-built. The intuition driving the frustration — "once we have the alignment it should be obvious, because the aligned datasets are so distinct from random alignments" — is not just right, it is measured: at the correct lock, 96.2 % of a pulse's DREAM triggers have a wall+plastic n_TOF partner within ±25 ns; at a wrong lock, 0.05 %. Three orders of magnitude of separation, available per single pulse.

The pipeline does not use that. It lets two weak instruments (count scans at ~50 ms tolerance) decide the alignment and uses the decisive instrument only as a tie-breaker, bolted on through exception handling — and in bolting it on, the rerun session wrote a fourth independent implementation of the coincidence measurement, whose docstrings record six separate bugs in two days, every one a rediscovery of a term the production clock fit already carries. That is where the "extremely hard time" is coming from. The struggle is architectural, not physical.

And the goal is closer than it looks: the 08-13 recovery campaign has 241 segments locally, median 94.9 % trigger-level efficiency, only 8 clock-QA FAILs — and every FAIL is a pre-run_79 special trigger configuration (run_42/43/51/64 scint and mesh scans). Post-run_79 the chain is already matching at fleet quality. Nobody can see that, because the accounting is per-trigger and per-segment, never per-pulse, and segments that fail never enter any QA denominator.

Where matching actually stands (2026-08-13)

campaignsegmentsoutcome
08-12 first slim campaign291 170 OK / 107 FAILED / 14 low-join — 25.7 % of beam lost, all to two of our own silent bugs (supercycle mislock, sliver bootstrap walk), both since diagnosed; DREAM data flawless
08-13 recovery (local mirror, dashboard 12:24)241 183 PASS / 50 WARN / 8 FAIL; median match efficiency 94.90 %, 5th pct 93.7 %. All 8 FAILs are run_42/43/51/64 — pre-run_79 scint/mesh-scan trigger configs. 49 of the 50 WARNs are lock-margin warnings on locks chosen by the intensity correlation, i.e. exactly the class a coincidence verification would settle.

So the question is no longer "can we match" — it is "prove every pulse is matched, and name the reason for each one that isn't." The current pipeline cannot answer that, for reasons audited below.

The chain as built — four layers, decisiveness inverted

layerwhat it matchestolerancediscriminating powerdecides?
1. pulse_matchDREAM cluster starts ↔ beam-intensity CSV 0.35 sDegenerate under the 39.6/43.2 s supercycle; ±120 s scan admits ±3 cycles that all match ~100 % of clusters yes — count margin ≥ 10, else Fisher-z on intensity correlation ≥ 3σ, else refuse
2. bunch_joinburst epochs ↔ PKUP psTime 50 msDegenerate on truncated pulse lists (boundary slivers, 26/26 lost pre-fix) yes — own δ-scan + margin guard + hint transfer + bootstrap-walk guard
3. coincidence arbiter (new, uncommitted) trigger times ↔ wall+plastic singles25 ns 96 % vs 0.05 % — three orders of magnitude per pulse only when layer 1 raises AmbiguousLock
4. clockfit / clock_qasame coincidence, full segment 25 nssameno — confirms after the product is written

The strongest instrument in the pipeline is consulted last, and only on appeal. Layers 1–2 carry between them: a count margin, a Fisher-z intensity arbitration, an AmbiguousLock exception that caches its own refusal (with a candidate list, with a regex fallback for parsing old cached messages), an evidence-override parameter with a two-value provenance label, a δ-margin guard, a cross-segment δ-hint transfer, and a bootstrap-walk guard. Every one of those is a patch on a weak instrument being asked to do a decisive job.

Findings

F1The inversion is only half done. The coincidence arbiter fires only on an AmbiguousLock. A count win at margin ≥ 10 still decides outright — and the margin study found 14 accepted segments at margin ≤ 2 in the first campaign ("healthy by coin flip"). The mislock class was born precisely from confident-looking counts under a repeating schedule. The decisive instrument costs ~8 bunches of IO per test; there is no reason any lock, however confident the count, should ship without it. One instrument should decide every segment, and it should be this one.
F2Four implementations of the same measurement — and the new one is a bug factory by construction. "Fraction of a pulse's triggers with a same-arm wall+plastic partner within ±25 ns" now exists in: (1) production clockfit+slim; (2) arbiter_measure.py, a ~250-line approximate re-derivation; (3) coincidence_arbiter.pulse_coincidence — zero callers, dead code; (4) an inline block newly added to clock_qa.py. The 0.80 pulse threshold is duplicated in two modules and absent from config.py.

arbiter_measure's own docstrings are a chronicle of why parallel implementations of solved problems fail. In two days it: rejected known-correct locks because the K≈1.1×10⁻⁴ clock-rate walk smeared the peak (production fits K); lost ~25 % of triggers to a nearest-in-absolute-time search centred on 0 instead of the +250 ns partner (production models the offset); read 75 % where production reads 96 % because it had no per-arm cable offsets (production carries them); under-scored pulses because 0.6 ppm per-bunch rate scatter is 48 ns across a burst (production fits per bunch); gutted the wall leg by measuring top/bottom offsets on its 8-bunch scoring sample instead of 150 (production separates calibration from scoring); and reported a plumbing NameError as "0 % coincidence on every candidate" through a bare except. Every single one is a term the production fit already had. The fix is not a seventh patch; it is deleting the parallel implementation and running the production join + clock fit on a sample of bunches.

F3Exception-driven state machine. AmbiguousLock is control flow: raised, caught, cached to JSON, re-raised from cache with a candidate list, text-parsed by regex when the cache predates the list (a fallback that silently dropped r=nan candidates — precisely the short segments that needed arbitration), then overridden by accept_offset_s which rewrites the cache under a different provenance label. Once the coincidence decides every lock, ambiguity is not an exceptional state — the enumerator returns candidates, the decider picks or refuses, and this entire machinery (cache versioning, .locks plumbing, _locks_from_text, the override/contradiction guards) deletes.
F4Two stacked count scans where zero are needed for deciding. Layer 1 scans ±120 s against the CSV; layer 2 then scans ±3 s against PKUP — but the CSV and PKUP are the same pulse stream separated by a rigid, measured constant (0.829 s NXCALS latency, MAD 5 ms). Scanning it per segment re-opens a degeneracy that a constant with a ±0.1 s sanity band closes. Both scans survive fine as candidate enumerators; neither should carry decision logic.
F5The accounting cannot answer the question being asked of it. "How many pulses were not confidently matched, and why?" fails at every level of the current bookkeeping:
  • Bursts with BunchNumber == −1 are dropped with zero accounting (slim.py:121) — a segment losing 30 % of its events is indistinguishable from a clean one in qa.json.
  • clockfit.efficiency excludes events in unfitted bunches from numerator and denominator — they vanish.
  • The new per-pulse check collapses to three scalars (n, unmatched, median_frac): no list of which pulses, no distribution, no reason split — though the wall-set/plastic-set ingredients to say wall-leg-missing vs plastic-leg-missing vs neither vs wrong-arm are computed and thrown away.
  • It only exists for segments that produced a product. The campaign's own README: "a mis-locked segment … simply writes no file — the QA never sees it." The 107 failures never entered any QA denominator.
  • The campaign ledger (slim_inventory_2026-08-12.csv) has no pulse column, and its generator script is not in the repo.

The simplification

A — one decision instrument

  1. pulse_match becomes an enumerator. Keep the wall-clock scan — it is good at producing a shortlist of ~6 candidate locks for free. It always returns the ranked candidate list; it never decides, never raises on ambiguity, and the intensity correlation demotes to a logged diagnostic. (Deletes: MARGIN_CLEAR/R_SIG decision logic, Fisher-z arbitration, ambiguity caching and re-raise, text parsing, override-contradiction guards.)
  2. The coincidence decides every segment, via production code. measure(offset) = standard join_events at that offset → sample ~8 spread bunches → standard pass1_candidates (top/bottom offsets measured once per n_TOF run on the proper 150-bunch sample) → standard clockfit → read its per-pulse coincidence fraction. Accept the first candidate ≥ 0.80 (the populations sit at 96 % and 0.05 %; the threshold cannot matter); refuse loudly if none passes. arbiter_measure's parallel physics (_nearest_dt, the walk fits, the hand-rolled arm offsets and per-bunch lines) deletes; the file shrinks to a thin sampling wrapper. The screening structure of coincidence_arbiter (rank, test best-first, stop at first pass) is sound and stays.
  3. Fix the CSV→PKUP constant. Replace bunch_join's ±3 s δ-scan with the measured 0.829 s latency ± a narrow band; the coincidence verification catches anything residual. The sliver class dies structurally (no scan against a truncated list), not by guard.
  4. Validation set before trusting it: the margin-0 exemplars (run_96/0001×224597 — recovered at 95.47 %; run_102/0003's dead tie), one boundary sliver (run_79/0002×224573), one healthy hour, one pre-run_79 scint-config run (expected to refuse — different trigger, the coincidence may legitimately be absent).

B — the pulse ledger (what the QA page should show)

Denominator: every DREAM burst of every sub-run, taken from the DREAM files alone — not from the products, not from the segments that happened to fit. Each burst ends in exactly one terminal state:

statemeaninghow it is determined
MATCHED≥ 80 % of its triggers wall+plastic coincident within ±25 nsthe existing clock_qa per-pulse check, extended to store per-pulse rows (bunch, n_triggers, fraction, per-leg counts)
LOW_COINCjoined to a bunch, coincidence below threshold — the real follow-up listsame rows, plus the leg breakdown (wall-only / plastic-only / neither / wrong-arm) already computable from the sets clock_qa builds and discards
EMPTY_PULSEPS delivered < 10×10¹⁰ p (diverted/dud)PKUP / CSV intensity — expected unmatched, not a failure
NTOF_NO_BUNCHpulse exists in the beam CSV but no n_TOF DAQ bunch exists — run reset, inter-run gap, DAQ offCSV × PKUP alone; needs no DREAM data and covers the runs' gaps exactly
TOO_FEW_TRIGGERSburst too small to judge at 80 %trigger count floor
SEGMENT_FAILEDthe sub-run never joined; carries the refusal reasonthe ledger walks the sub-run list, so these bursts stay in the denominator instead of vanishing

Dashboard top section, per sub-run: bursts, matched %, one column per reason class, drill-down to the individual unmatched pulses. Headline number: "N of M pulses since run_79 confidently matched" against the 99 % target — computed over the full denominator, so it can only be wrong by being honest.

What honestly remains unmatched

With the ledger in place the residual should be entirely physical and enumerable: n_TOF run resets and inter-run gaps (NTOF_NO_BUNCH), diverted/empty pulses, the early-run DAQ divert/dead-bunch pathologies, and the pre-run_79 trigger configurations. Everything else — every LOW_COINC and SEGMENT_FAILED pulse after run_79 — is a genuine follow-up item with its reason attached, which is exactly the list the QA page exists to show.

Addendum — outcome, same day (2026-08-13 evening)

The audit was implemented the same day, jointly by two sessions (this one and the matching-rerun session, which validated and extended its own instrument in parallel). Numbers below are the rerun session's, checked against its condor logs; the ledger and the measured δ are this session's.

99 of the 112 unmatched segments are resolved by letting the coincidence choose the lock (accepted-lock score min 83 %, median 95 %, mean 1.49 candidates tested per segment). And the audit's central claim is now a campaign-wide measurement: the highest score any measured wrong lock reached, across every candidate evaluation in the campaign, is 0.00 %. The 0.20–0.80 "ambiguous band" was never entered once. The separation is not a threshold question; there is nothing near the bar from below.

  • The δ constant is measured and the narrowing is regression-clean. All 241 fitted segments: median 0.8290 s, MAD 0.1 ms, extremes ±11 ms of median. Confining bunch_join's search to 0.8290 ± 0.1 s (δ still fitted from matched pairs; an edge guard refuses if the lock lands within 10 % of the band edge) reproduced all four independently-established reference locks to the digit, and structurally removes the degenerate ambiguity of the second count scan.
  • The honest classification of the 13 remaining refusals (after fixing a measured-zero vs never-measured conflation whose repair changed the accounting and not one outcome — 17 resolved before, 17 after): 6 genuine no's (every candidate measured, all at 0 %), 1 NoLock (nothing enumerated), 3 blocked solely by pulse_match's confident-selection guard — which the enumerator refactor removes, since there is no longer a "confident automatic selection" for an override to contradict — and 3 no-overlap segments: they first surfaced as δ band-edge refusals (all five edge blocks at exactly band-start, +0.7290 s), and the mechanism was then reproduced from first principles — a synthetic no-overlap sub-run lands on +0.7290 with 0 matched bursts, a real overlap on +0.7800 with 200, a 4-burst sliver is not refused. Two of the three sit on the 8-12 campaign's independent list of dark DREAM runs. The scan now refuses no-overlap by name (best in-band count below a 3-burst floor) before the edge guard can fire, so this class is an absence of data, not a gate; per-segment confirmation rides with the re-slim. Of 36 blocked candidate evaluations, 31 were the selection guard, 5 the band edge.
  • Cost is a non-issue: median 63 s per candidate measurement (min 7 s, max 682 s, n = 76); the re-slim's 30–45 GB copy dominates, not the arbitration.
  • The contract and the ledger are landed: single-source config.PULSE_MIN_FRAC; per-pulse leg arrays in clock_qa.json with the partition asserted element-wise; burst_map.json carrying every burst including the unmatched (previously dropped uncounted); the burst census written in-job before the join can refuse; machine-readable arbiter refusals distinguishing "no lock reached 80 %" from "the coincidence never got to decide". The ledger (slim_pipeline/pulse_ledger.py) classifies every burst into the terminal states of §B, and its campaign aggregator refuses to let a sub-run silently leave the denominator — a missing census is a red banner, not an absence.

Final results — the ledger headline (2026-08-13, end of day)

All three follow-ups executed same-day: the re-slim ran (54/54 runs, 179 recovered segments shipped with full sidecars), the enumerator refactor is done (the confident-selection guard is gone; disagreements are recorded, not discarded), and the parallel measurement was deleted after earning it — an A/B on all six known locks had the production-clockfit measurer winning 5 of 6 and tighter (96–98 % vs 87–98 %), rejection identical and absolute. 306 lines of parallel physics removed.

Every pulse since run_79 is classified. 265,693 of 272,212 = 97.61 % confidently matched (98.05 % excluding pulses where n_TOF's DAQ was not recording). Presented alongside the instrument's number — 99.804 % of stat090 pulses that reached a product (269,097/269,626, 368 segments) — the difference between the two is the denominator this audit existed to expose: 3,832 pulses in failed segments (dark runs, genuine no-coincidence segments, no-overlap slivers), 1,235 in n_TOF inter-run gaps, 928 never attempted, 523 genuinely below the coincidence bar. Cross-checked independently: the ledger's census route and the per-pulse-array route agree on the follow-up count to the pulse (520 = 520) and on MATCHED exactly, after two accounting defects the comparison itself exposed (a beam-CSV logging gap mis-classing 30 join-vouched pulses; failed sub-runs hidden outside the denominator).

  • The misses are physics now, not bookkeeping: of unmatched stat090 triggers campaign-wide, 52 % are wall-leg-absent and 38 % plastic-leg-absent — 90 % single-leg inefficiency, roughly 4:3 wall-present:plastic-present — with neither at only 4.3 %, so these are not dead triggers. wrong_arm is 5.4 %, the one category that would indicate mapping/geometry rather than efficiency; watch it per-arm.
  • A production reader bug found and measured to zero impact: ntof_io's psTime repair used a searchsorted insertion point as a match — one path crashed (run 224498), the other silently mis-dated a missing bunch from its neighbour. Fixed; and the before/after ledger diff across 548 sub-runs shows 0 state flips and 0 burst→bunch reassignments attributable to it — the silent half never bit this campaign. Measured on both axes, not argued.
  • The largest failed block recovered: run_156/stat090_0022 (dark-run family, 542-pulse failure) came back matched when its product landed — SEGMENT_FAILED is a statement about processing, never about the beam.
  • The refactored enumerator's acceptance test closed the loop, on real data: all three guard-blocked segments produce OK products at fleet efficiency (94.5–97.2 %), every lock coincidence-chosen. The precise confirmation: run_139/stat090_0010's correct lock, +13.58 s, is the exact candidate the pre-refactor guard refused to let anyone measure — with the count scan confidently pointing at −96.82 s (margin 25) — so the weak instrument was not merely weak, it was confidently wrong, and it had veto power over the strong one. That is the audit's central claim demonstrated end to end rather than argued. (Campaign provenance is pre-refactor products plus these recovered segments; the refactor changes which lock is chosen only where the guard was blocking, and both instruments agreeing to the pulse everywhere else is the evidence it blocked nowhere else.)
  • Residue, honestly: 53 sub-runs remain unclassified (19 calibration modes with no product, never measured; the rest await censuses or products).
